name: Zheng Fan
current_role: Non-executive director, Li Auto Inc. (since Oct 2020)
profile: Fan Zheng is a co-founder of car portal Autohome, where he was vice president in charge of technology operations until 2016. He is a shareholder and non-executive (independent) director of EV maker Li Auto, founded by his longtime partner Li Xiang, which listed on Nasdaq in 2020 and in Hong Kong in 2021.
interesting_fact: His partnership with Li Auto CEO Li Xiang spans three companies: PCPOP.com, Autohome and now Li Auto, where he sits on the audit, compensation and nominating committees.
deep_cut_fact: Before Autohome he co-founded and was VP of PCPOP.com (2000-2005), the PC-hardware review site Li Xiang started as a teenager; Fan graduated from Hebei University of Science and Technology in 1999.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is via Li Auto IR. Sources differ on Autohome start date (1999 vs 2005).

name: Wong Kwong Yu
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, GOME Retail Holdings (HKEX: 0493)
profile: Wong Kwong Yu (Huang Guangyu) founded GOME, which grew from a single Beijing stall into China's largest consumer-electronics retail chain and made him China's richest man in the mid-2000s. He was convicted in 2010 and paroled in 2020; since his release he has sought to revive GOME's retail and e-commerce business.
interesting_fact: Time named him China's richest man in 2005; he had started GOME as a teenager with his brother after moving to Beijing from Shantou.
deep_cut_fact: GOME's first outlet opened on 1 January 1987 in a rented ~100 sq m shop on Zhushikou Street near Qianmen in Beijing; the 'GOME' (Guomei, 'beautiful country') brand name was only adopted in 1993.
notes: Highly sensitive history (2010 conviction, parole 2020); GOME is financially distressed. A general address info@gome.com.hk appears only on third-party quote pages (etnet), not verified on company site. Born Zeng Junlie, 1969, Shantou.

name: Qin Long
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and controlling shareholder (~43%), Qingdao Sentury Tire Co. (SZSE: 002984)
profile: Qin Long founded Qingdao Sentury Tire in 2007, building it from a manual tire plant in Qingdao into a listed maker of passenger, motorsport and aircraft tires with factories in Qingdao, Thailand and elsewhere. Sentury listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020; he directly and indirectly controls about 43% of the company.
interesting_fact: Sentury is one of the few Chinese firms making aircraft tires, alongside motorsport tires, and it pursued an overseas-factory strategy with a heavily automated plant in Rayong, Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: Qin was reportedly the only one in his management team backing a fully automated 'Dream Factory'; after automating Qingdao's green-tire handling (utilisation rose from 72% to 96.5%) he copied it to Thailand. Quote: 'I have orders and I will lose the customers if I cannot deliver the tires.'
notes: IR email belongs to the board secretary's office (board secretary Wang Qian). Chairman title last explicitly confirmed in 2025 filings; 2026 interim report lists him as legal representative and controller. Cimcorp source is a vendor case study.

name: Wang Qian
current_role: Founder and CEO, X Square Robot (Zibianliang Jiqiren), Shenzhen
profile: Wang Qian, a Tsinghua and USC-trained robotics researcher, ran a quant fund in the US before closing it in 2023 to found X Square Robot in Shenzhen. The embodied-AI startup builds general-purpose robot foundation models (WALL-A, open-sourced WALL-OSS) and reached a valuation above US$2.8bn in 2026, with backers including Alibaba, ByteDance, Meituan and Xiaomi.
interesting_fact: He argues humanoid robots doing repetitive factory work are 'just a PR stunt' and that the field should focus on generalisation; X Square raised four consecutive rounds to pass a $2.8bn valuation by mid-2026.
deep_cut_fact: As a researcher he was among the early adopters of attention mechanisms in neural networks, publishing at the same 2014 conference as Google's early attention paper; after leaving robotics for finance he said 'I couldn't sleep for nights. I regretted not pursuing robotics full time.'
notes: Highly relevant to an AI/compute-themed podcast (embodied AI foundation models). No published personal net worth found; the list source is not Forbes. Pandaily attention-mechanism claim is from a paywalled profile (visible portion).

name: Wang Weiyao
current_role: Founder and chairman, Jiangsu World Group (Wode / 沃得集团), Danyang, Jiangsu
profile: Wang Weiyao (王伟耀, b. 1963, Danyang) founded World Group, a Danyang-based machinery conglomerate whose World Agricultural Machinery unit is one of China's largest makers of rice combine harvesters; it also makes forging presses (World Precision Machinery), construction and garden machinery, auto parts and develops property.
interesting_fact: He built World Group from a small textile-machinery accessories workshop founded in 1988 into a group with ~20,000 staff; its harvesters are sold across China and exported to dozens of countries.
deep_cut_fact: After finishing Picheng Middle School in 1982, his first venture was the Danyang Textile Machinery Accessories Factory (1988); he later added crankshaft, filter and kitchen-equipment plants before moving into combine harvesters in 1997. He holds an MBA from Nanjing University of Science and Technology and a CEIBS EMBA.
notes: Identity inferred from 'World' source-of-wealth label (no Forbes bio in input); Wang Weiyao of World (Wode) Group is the only strong match. Very private; Chinese-language outreach via group website contact page likely best.

name: Li Shijiang
current_role: Director and actual controller of Do-Fluoride New Materials (SZSE: 002407); chairman of parent Jiaozuo Do-Fluoride Industrial Group
profile: Li Shijiang (b. 1950, Wen County, Henan) turned the state-owned Jiaozuo Cryolite Factory into Do-Fluoride (DFD), a leading maker of fluorine chemicals and of lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF6), the key salt in lithium-ion battery electrolyte. He chaired the listed company from 2007 until handing over the chair in Dec 2025; he remains a director and controls the parent group.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he went to Japan to buy LiPF6 production technology, was turned away, then assembled his own team, which spent about eight years cracking the process, making DFD one of the world's largest LiPF6 suppliers for EV batteries.
deep_cut_fact: Before chemicals he served five years in the PLA Second Artillery (1968-73), then rose through the Wen County fertilizer plant (equipment and technical sections, petrochemical plant director) and a paper mill; he also chairs the council of Henan Polytechnic University's New Materials Industry College.
notes: Age 76. Strong battery-supply-chain angle. Military-service detail is from Chinese media profiles; the annual report confirms the career path. Listed company chairmanship changed hands in Dec 2025.

name: Zhang Ying
current_role: Founding managing partner, MPCi (formerly Matrix Partners China / 经纬创投), Beijing
profile: Zhang Ying (David Zhang) co-founded Matrix Partners China in 2008 after running WI Harper Group's China business, building one of China's most active early-stage VC firms (now branded MPCi) with early bets across internet, consumer and healthcare. The firm now focuses on software, energy technology, advanced manufacturing and consumer.
interesting_fact: MPCi says it prefers to be the first institutional investor and largest non-management shareholder in a startup, and that it cares more about founders' 'intellect, track record and potential than your PowerPoint skills.'
deep_cut_fact: Born in Shanghai in 1973, he emigrated to the US with his parents in 1987, studied biology and later earned a master's in biotechnology and business at Northwestern, and started in finance at Salomon Smith Barney and ABN AMRO Capital before moving into venture capital.
notes: 'Zhang Ying' is a very common name; matched on 'Matrix' source of wealth (no Forbes bio in input). Deep-cut details come from CompassList (archive as of 2021). Web search budget ran out mid-lane; firm-level 2026 status not re-verified. MPCi energy-tech focus is a good podcast hook.

name: Randall M Ruhlman
current_role: Major shareholder (~23% beneficial owner) of Preformed Line Products (Nasdaq: PLPC); former PLP director
profile: Randall M. Ruhlman is a member of the family that controls Preformed Line Products, the Mayfield Village, Ohio maker of hardware for power-transmission, distribution and telecom lines founded by his grandfather Thomas F. Peterson. His brother Robert G. Ruhlman is chairman and CEO; Randall holds about 23% of the shares beneficially, largely via family trusts where he is co-trustee or co-trust advisor.

deep_cut_fact: He has run his own race team: PLP's 2003 proxy lists him as president of Ruhlman Motorsports, a race car team, since 1987, with PLP as a sponsor. He sat on PLP's board from 1998.

name: Yang Le
current_role: Chairman and co-actual controller, Anhui Jinhe Industrial Co. (SZSE: 002597)
profile: Yang Le (b. 1989) chairs Anhui Jinhe Industrial, a Chuzhou-based chemical group that is a major producer of sweeteners and flavour ingredients such as acesulfame-K (Ace-K), sucralose and maltol, alongside basic and fine chemicals. He joined in 2013 and rose from assistant to the GM to vice chairman and chairman; he is one of the company's two actual controllers.
interesting_fact: Jinhe's zero-calorie sweeteners (Ace-K, sucralose) go into soft drinks and foods worldwide; the company is expanding into natural sweeteners and functional sugars.
deep_cut_fact: Born in May 1989, he is among the youngest chairmen of a Shenzhen-listed chemical group; beyond sweeteners he also chairs Anhui Liguang Electronic Materials and Nanjing Jinhe Yikang Biotechnology.
notes: Identity matched on 'Jinhe' = Anhui Jinhe Industrial (no Forbes bio in input). Facts from 2025 annual report. Low international media profile.

name: He Xianning
current_role: Founder and former chairman (2012-Mar 2026) of Shenzhen Anche Technologies (SZSE: 300572); remains a significant shareholder
profile: He Xianning (b. 1970) founded Anche Technologies, a Shenzhen provider of motor-vehicle safety and emissions inspection equipment and systems, now also serving new-energy vehicle testing and auto aftermarket services. He led it as GM and chairman and took it public; in 2025-26 he transferred control to sensor maker QST (Shanghai Xirui) and stepped down as chairman in March 2026.
interesting_fact: A radio engineering graduate of the University of Science and Technology of China, he helped draft several Chinese national/industry standards for vehicle testing, including brake test benches (GB/T13564-2005) and chassis dynamometers (JT/T445-2008).
deep_cut_fact: He started as an engineer at Shenzhen Dalei Industrial (1996-2003) before founding Anche Technology in 2003; he is vice president of the China Automobile Maintenance Equipment Industry Association.
notes: Control of Anche passed to QST (Shanghai Xirui Technology) in Feb 2026; he left the chair on 3 Mar 2026, so company IR may no longer be a direct route to him. Very low public profile.

name: Wu Yi-Gui
current_role: Chairman of USI Corporation (Taiwan, TWSE-listed) and Group CEO of USI Group
profile: Wu Yi-Gui (吳亦圭, also known as Quintin Wu) chairs USI Corporation and runs the USI Group, a Taipei-based petrochemical and plastics group (polyethylene, EVA, PVC via China General Plastics) with investments in electronics, logistics, green energy and venture capital. USI Corp was founded in 1965 and built Taiwan's first LDPE plant in Kaohsiung.
interesting_fact: USI's EVA resin is used in solar-panel encapsulation film, where the company says it holds a leading position in quality and technology, tying the group to the solar build-out.
notes: Input lists country as China but the matching 'USI' chairman 吳亦圭 is in Taiwan (USI Corp board page: https://www.usife.com.tw/zh-tw/dirAbout/frmAbout4.aspx). Mapping 'Wu Yi-Gui' to 吳亦圭 and the English name Quintin Wu was not confirmed (web search budget exhausted).

name: Tang Jian
current_role: Founder, chairman and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen Jieshun Science and Technology (SZSE: 002609)
profile: Tang Jian (b. 1956) founded Jieshun in Shenzhen in 1992 and has led it since, first as executive director and GM and now as chairman. Jieshun began with parking and access-control hardware and has become a smart-parking platform spanning hardware, cloud software, parking operations and its 'Jie Parking' (捷停车) app.
interesting_fact: Jieshun's Jie Parking unit was among the first smart-parking companies to list data assets on the Shenzhen Data Exchange, an early example of a Chinese firm trading its operational data as an asset.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded the Shenzhen Jieshun Leshan Poverty Alleviation Foundation, which runs student-aid, 'warm winter' relief and 'little desk' / books-to-schools projects for rural schools; he holds a CEIBS EMBA.
notes: Facts from Jieshun's 2025 annual report. Low international profile; Chinese-language outreach via the board secretary's office is the practical route.

name: Lyu Xinmin
current_role: Chairman, general manager and controlling shareholder, Shanghai Yongguan Adhesive Products / Yongguan New Materials (SSE: 603681)
profile: Lyu Xinmin (吕新民, b. 1971), from Cangnan county in Zhejiang, founded Shanghai Yongguan Adhesive Products in 2002 and built it into Yongguan New Materials (YG Tape), a Shanghai-listed maker of adhesive tapes and adhesives such as cloth-based, masking and specialty tapes, with production bases in Shanghai and Jiangxi.
interesting_fact: Before founding Yongguan he ran a small tape factory, the Cangnan Andeli Tape Factory, in his home county; two decades later his company is a listed tape maker that exports globally.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the chamber of commerce of Zaoxi town in Cangnan, his home area, and is executive vice-president of the Shanghai Cangnan Chamber of Commerce and of the Fuzhou (Jiangxi) Hakka Merchants Investment Enterprise Association.
notes: Facts from the 2025 annual report. No international media profile; outreach via the board secretary's office (IR email).

name: Zhu Zhigang
current_role: Chairman, controlling shareholder and legal representative, Zhejiang Jinke Tom Culture Industry (Tom Cat / 汤姆猫, SZSE: 300459)
profile: Zhu Zhigang (b. 1965) controls Jinke Tom Culture, which owns Slovenian studio Outfit7 and the 'Talking Tom & Friends' franchise of casual mobile games and animation. He has chaired the company since January 2021; it is now pushing the IP into AI hardware such as the Tom Cat AI robot.
interesting_fact: The Talking Tom & Friends games have passed 26 billion cumulative downloads, and the cartoons have been translated into 32 languages; Sensor Tower ranks the franchise at the top of global mobile-game IP download charts.
deep_cut_fact: Under the slogan of turning 'Talking Tom' into 'Chatting Tom', the company has launched an LLM-powered Tom Cat AI robot for families and a portable 'Tom Cat AI' device since Dec 2024. Zhu, a Macau national, holds economist and engineer titles and is an adjunct professor at Zhejiang University of Technology.
notes: Filings note pledged shares and some of his shares auctioned in 2025; avoid wealth topics. The AI-companion angle is a good hook. Facts from the 2025 annual report.

name: Atul Chordia
current_role: Founder and chairman, Panchshil Realty (Pune); chairman and executive director, Ventive Hospitality (NSE/BSE-listed)
profile: Atul Chordia founded Pune developer Panchshil Realty in 2002, building office parks such as EON Free Zone and World Trade Center Pune, luxury homes (yoopune, Trump Towers Pune) and hotels. His hospitality JV with Blackstone, Ventive Hospitality (JW Marriott and Ritz-Carlton Pune, resorts in the Maldives and Sri Lanka), listed in India in Dec 2024 after a ~Rs1,600 crore IPO.
interesting_fact: Panchshil has repeatedly partnered with global capital: Merrill Lynch invested in 2004, it jointly bought Mumbai's Express Towers with Blackstone in 2014, and it teamed with Singapore's GIC on the EON West office project in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: One of Panchshil's first landmark projects was Tech Park One, completed for IBM in Pune in 2003. Chordia, who studied commerce at Pune's Ness Wadia College, received the college society's 'Eminent Wadian' award in 2024.
notes: Good fit for a data-center/real-estate angle: Panchshil is a major Pune office/IT-park developer. No personal social accounts verified (web search budget exhausted).

name: Shen Guangqian
current_role: Former chairman and president (to March 2018) and large shareholder of Beijing Leadman Biochemistry (SZSE: 300289); current role not found
profile: Shen Guangqian (b. 1961) led Beijing Leadman Biochemistry, an in-vitro diagnostics maker of biochemical reagents, as chairman and president and took it public on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2012. He resigned in March 2018; control of Leadman has since passed to Guangzhou High-tech Zone Science & Technology Holding, a state-owned investor.
interesting_fact: Under him Leadman built a reference laboratory to ISO 17025/ISO 15195 standards, unusual for a Chinese diagnostics firm, to make its own key raw materials and reduce reliance on imports.
